correctness.rationale: An acyclic generator is upper triangular. The matrix-function divided-difference path expansion has nonnegative factors because f and its first three derivatives on the negative real axis are nonnegative; Hermite--Genocchi gives positivity for every path of <=3 edges, for every h. For arbitrary <=4-state generators, the first coefficients 1,1,1/2,0,-1/4 plus shortest-walk sign yield positive sufficiently small nonzero reachable entries, including the distance-three case with (Q^4)_ij<0. The five-state exact inverse has absorbing-column remainders B1,B2,B3 positive and B4=h^4P(h)/D(h)^4; P strictly increases from -4 to infinity. The actual package verify.py checked exact identities and 192 supplementary rational DAG samples; finite experiments not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact order-two L-stable map is proposed in 2026 for numerical probability evolution where negative states are unacceptable. The theorem isolates a natural graph-topological safe class that works in any number of states at all positive steps, proves a minimum state count for small-step sign loss even under exact mass conservation, and gives the complete algebraic step window for the minimum witness. This provides a concrete integrity benchmark for path-limited conservative discretizations and clarifies why A/L-stability plus mass conservation do not imply nonnegative transition matrices. It is not merely a numerical table or an arbitrary parameter slice.
